summary: Perry County Aermotor MC-39 tower dated 1949 and registered in 2011; the Alabama Forestry Commission is named as administrator, and no current status was found.

facts.agency: Alabama Forestry Commission (administrator and cooperator, per register)

events.note: Built field on the register; the builder is not named
Registered January 3, 2011; nominated by Thomas Kaufmann

evidence.supports: on a high point in Perry County; 100-foot tower
evidence.quote: On a high point in Perry County stands the 100' Joyce Hill Fire Tower.
It is an Aermotor MC-39 with 7'x7' cab.

evidence.supports: Alabama Forestry Commission named as administrator and cooperator
MC-39 was the most common steel lookout model in Alabama's forests
evidence.quote: The most common steel lookout tower model in
was the Aermotor MC-39, followed by the LS-40 version

sources.title: Thomas Kaufmann keeping Alabama's historic lookout towers

notes_for_editor: Only one source has substance: the NHLR page. The 1949 date is from its Built field and names no builder. Two web searches and the cached FFLOS and Wikidata pages gave nothing about this tower. The record's status 'standing' is not stated by the register; no current status or visit report was found. The record's material 'steel' is not stated for this tower. The story uses the 1819 News remark about MC-39 as a steel model in Alabama, so the material claim stays inferred. No staffing, fire, access or condition information was found. Height 30.5 m is converted from the 100 ft overall height; cab floor height is not given. Suggested check: Alabama Forestry Commission records or Perry County historical sources.
